programme.name: Monitoring & Observability Follow Along
programme.requiredOutcome: Configure CloudWatch alarms, a custom application metric, CloudWatch Logs Insights queries, AWS X-Ray tracing and a custom Amazon EventBridge event bus; connect them through an observable Lambda workload; generate normal and controlled-error signals; verify the complete event-to-metric/log/alarm/trace flow; then safely remove only the fa-monitoring training resources.
programme.estimatedLearnerFlow: Use the existing administrator account throughout. Console instructions and AWS CloudShell commands are both provided. Do not create separate long-lived CLI credentials.
completionDefinition: The learner works from the existing administrator account in eu-west-2 and uses CloudShell for CLI work.
fa-monitoring-lambda-role grants logging, X-Ray and only FA/Monitoring custom metric publication.
fa-monitoring-observer runs with X-Ray Active tracing and logs to /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer.
fa-monitoring-bus and fa-monitoring-rule deliver matching TrainingEvent events to the Lambda function.
Successful events publish FA/Monitoring ProcessedEvents and produce OBSERVABILITY_EVENT status=processed logs.
CloudWatch contains one custom-metric alarm and one Lambda Errors alarm.
One deliberate forceError event produces a Lambda error, forced_error log record and observable error signal without retries.
Logs Insights queries return both detail and grouped status results.
X-Ray trace summaries can be inspected for sampled Lambda invocations.
All fa-monitoring cloud resources and CloudShell helper files are removed while the administrator account remains unchanged.

authoringBasis.uploadedStandard: AI_Follow_Along_Steps(1).txt portable offline authoring workflow and the established Study Tracker offline manuscript contract.
rulesApplied: Use the existing administrator account; do not instruct the learner to switch to a different privileged account.
Use AWS CloudShell instead of creating separate long-lived CLI credentials.
Assume no fa-monitoring infrastructure already exists.
Provide complete Console and CloudShell routes, expected results and verification checks.
Every task sourceIds entry is mirrored by source usedByTaskIds.
Use only official AWS documentation in the source list.
Perform manual reverse-dependency cleanup and preserve the administrator account.

doNotClaim: AWS or Supabase connection by the external authoring process
boundaries.destructiveSafety: Delete only the exact fa-monitoring training resources and helper files created by this Follow Along. The existing administrator account remains unchanged.

warnings.cost: CloudWatch custom metrics, alarms, Logs Insights queries, log storage, Lambda invocations, X-Ray traces and EventBridge events can incur charges. The lab uses small controlled volumes and one-day log retention, but current AWS pricing should be reviewed before starting.
warnings.safety: Use only the existing administrator account and the exact fa-monitoring names. The controlled error is an intentional Lambda exception in the disposable training function and EventBridge target retries are disabled.
warnings.credentials: The lab uses AWS CloudShell under the administrator console session and does not require creating a separate long-lived access key or local CLI profile.
warnings.region: All AWS resources in this Follow Along are created in eu-west-2. Keep the Console and CloudShell Region aligned to eu-west-2.

tasks.title: Verify the administrator account, Region and CloudShell
tasks.goal: Confirm the learner is signed in with the existing administrator account, select eu-west-2 and open AWS CloudShell.
tasks.whyItMatters: The lab creates IAM, Lambda, CloudWatch, X-Ray and EventBridge resources, so the working identity and Region must be known before anything is created.
tasks.examRelevance: Operational visibility depends on configuring monitoring in the same Region as the workload being observed.
warnings: Use the existing administrator account for this Follow Along. Do not create separate long-lived CLI credentials.

browserRoute.instruction: Sign in to the AWS Management Console using the existing administrator account for the training environment.
Open the account menu and verify this is the intended personal training account.
Use the Region selector and choose Europe (London), eu-west-2.
Open AWS CloudShell from the console toolbar.
Confirm the CloudShell prompt opens successfully before continuing.

cliRoute.title: Verify the CloudShell identity and Region
cliRoute.content:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure get region
export AWS_REGION=eu-west-2
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=eu-west-2
printf 'Region: %s\n' "$AWS_REGION"

expectedResults: The console is using the existing administrator account.
The selected Region is eu-west-2.
CloudShell is authenticated to the same AWS account without creating a separate access key.

verificationChecks.check: get-caller-identity returns the expected training account.
AWS_REGION prints eu-west-2.
CloudShell is ready for the later CLI routes.

troubleshooting.fix: Switch the console Region to eu-west-2, reopen CloudShell, and export AWS_REGION and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION as shown.

tasks.title: Create the Lambda execution role for logs, traces and custom metrics
tasks.goal: Create fa-monitoring-lambda-role with Lambda trust, CloudWatch Logs access, X-Ray trace publishing and a namespace-restricted custom metric permission.
tasks.whyItMatters: The function needs separate permissions to write logs, publish traces and submit its own metric data.
tasks.examRelevance: SAA-C03 expects least-privilege IAM roles for AWS services rather than embedding credentials in application code.
warnings: Do not attach broad administrator permissions to the Lambda execution role.

browserRoute.instruction: Open IAM > Roles > Create role.
Trusted entity type: AWS service.
Use case: Lambda.
Attach AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole.
Attach AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess.
Role name: fa-monitoring-lambda-role.
Create the role.
Open the new role > Permissions > Add permissions > Create inline policy.
Choose JSON and paste the supplied fa-monitoring-metric-policy.json.
Name the inline policy fa-monitoring-metric-policy and create it.
Confirm the role has the two AWS managed policies plus the one inline policy and no broad administrator policy.

cliRoute.title: CLI alternative - create the execution role

expectedResults: fa-monitoring-lambda-role exists.
Lambda can write CloudWatch Logs and X-Ray trace data.
cloudwatch:PutMetricData is restricted to namespace FA/Monitoring.

verificationChecks.check: The trust principal is lambda.amazonaws.com.
AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole is attached.
AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess is attached.
The inline metric policy contains cloudwatch:namespace = FA/Monitoring.

tasks.title: Create the Lambda log group with one-day retention
tasks.goal: Create /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer before invocation and set retention to one day.
tasks.whyItMatters: Explicit retention prevents temporary training logs from remaining indefinitely after the exercise.
tasks.examRelevance: CloudWatch Logs centralizes application logs and retention settings control how long log data remains.

browserRoute.instruction: Open CloudWatch > Logs > Log groups.
Choose Create log group.
Log group name: /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer.
Create the log group.
Open the log group and change Retention setting to 1 day.
Confirm the exact log group name and retention period.

cliRoute.title: Create and verify the log group
cliRoute.content:
aws logs create-log-group   --log-group-name /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer   --tags TrainingPrefix=fa-monitoring

aws logs put-retention-policy   --log-group-name /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer   --retention-in-days 1

aws logs describe-log-groups   --log-group-name-prefix /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer   --query "logGroups[0].{Name:logGroupName,RetentionDays:retentionInDays}"

expectedResults: The exact Lambda log group exists.
Retention is set to one day.

verificationChecks.check: Log group name is /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer.
RetentionDays is 1.

tasks.title: Create the observer Lambda and enable X-Ray Active tracing
tasks.goal: Deploy fa-monitoring-observer, enable Active tracing and use the supplied Python to log events and publish ProcessedEvents.
tasks.whyItMatters: One small function gives the lab a single workload that emits logs, metrics, traces and controlled errors.
tasks.examRelevance: CloudWatch observes runtime behavior while X-Ray provides request traces and service-level latency/error visibility.
warnings: The forceError path is deliberately used later to create one controlled Lambda failure for observability testing.

browserRoute.instruction: Open Lambda > Functions > Create function.
Choose Author from scratch.
Function name: fa-monitoring-observer.
Runtime: Python 3.12.
Architecture: x86_64.
Under execution role choose Use an existing role and select fa-monitoring-lambda-role.
Create the function.
Replace the default code with the supplied lambda_function.py and choose Deploy.
Open Configuration > Monitoring and operations tools > Edit.
Enable Lambda service traces / AWS X-Ray Active tracing and save.
Open Configuration > General configuration and set Timeout to 15 seconds.
Confirm the function is not attached to a VPC.

cliRoute.title: CLI alternative - package and create the function
cliRoute.content:
cat > lambda_function.py <<'PY'
import boto3
import json

cloudwatch = boto3.client("cloudwatch")

def lambda_handler(event, context):
    detail = event.get("detail", {})
    message = detail.get("message", "no-message")
    force_error = bool(detail.get("forceError", False))

    if force_error:
        print(
            f"OBSERVABILITY_EVENT status=forced_error "
            f"request_id={context.aws_request_id} message={message}"
        )
        raise RuntimeError("Intentional training error for observability verification")

    cloudwatch.put_metric_data(
        Namespace="FA/Monitoring",
        MetricData=[
            {
                "MetricName": "ProcessedEvents",
                "Dimensions": [
                    {
                        "Name": "FunctionName",
                        "Value": "fa-monitoring-observer"
                    }
                ],
                "Value": 1,
                "Unit": "Count"
            }
        ]
    )

    print(
        f"OBSERVABILITY_EVENT status=processed "
        f"request_id={context.aws_request_id} message={message}"
    )

    return {
        "statusCode": 200,
        "processed": True,
        "message": message
    }

PY

zip -q fa-monitoring-observer.zip lambda_function.py
ROLE_ARN=$(aws iam get-role   --role-name fa-monitoring-lambda-role   --query 'Role.Arn'   --output text)

sleep 10

aws lambda create-function   --function-name fa-monitoring-observer   --runtime python3.12   --handler lambda_function.lambda_handler   --role "$ROLE_ARN"   --zip-file fileb://fa-monitoring-observer.zip   --timeout 15   --memory-size 128   --tracing-config Mode=Active   --tags TrainingPrefix=fa-monitoring

aws lambda get-function-configuration   --function-name fa-monitoring-observer   --query '{FunctionName:FunctionName,Runtime:Runtime,Tracing:TracingConfig.Mode,Timeout:Timeout,Role:Role}'

codeBlocks.title: Lambda observer code

expectedResults: fa-monitoring-observer is Active.
Tracing mode is Active.
The function writes OBSERVABILITY_EVENT log lines and publishes FA/Monitoring ProcessedEvents for successful events.

verificationChecks.check: Function name is fa-monitoring-observer.
Runtime is Python 3.12.
TracingConfig.Mode is Active.
Execution role is fa-monitoring-lambda-role.

troubleshooting.symptom: CreateFunction reports that the role cannot be assumed
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the role trust is for lambda.amazonaws.com, wait briefly for IAM propagation, then retry.

tasks.title: Create the custom EventBridge event bus
tasks.goal: Create fa-monitoring-bus in eu-west-2 as the dedicated application event bus for the lab.
tasks.whyItMatters: A custom event bus separates application events from the default bus and gives the lab a clear event-driven boundary.
tasks.examRelevance: EventBridge routes events using event buses, rules and targets.

browserRoute.instruction: Open Amazon EventBridge in eu-west-2.
Choose Event buses > Create event bus.
Name: fa-monitoring-bus.
Keep the default encryption choice for this observability lab.
Add tag TrainingPrefix = fa-monitoring.
Create the event bus.
Open it and confirm the exact name and ARN.

cliRoute.title: Create and verify the event bus
cliRoute.content:
aws events create-event-bus   --name fa-monitoring-bus   --tags Key=TrainingPrefix,Value=fa-monitoring

aws events describe-event-bus --name fa-monitoring-bus

expectedResults: fa-monitoring-bus exists in eu-west-2.
Its ARN contains event-bus/fa-monitoring-bus.

verificationChecks.check: The event bus name is exactly fa-monitoring-bus.
The event bus is in eu-west-2.

tasks.title: Create the EventBridge rule and Lambda target
tasks.goal: Create fa-monitoring-rule on the custom bus, match only the training source/detail type and route matching events to fa-monitoring-observer.
tasks.whyItMatters: EventBridge rules filter events before targets are invoked, so only the intended event shape reaches the workload.
tasks.examRelevance: Rules use event patterns to route selected events to targets such as Lambda.
warnings: The target retry count is deliberately set to zero so the later controlled error creates one failure rather than repeated training failures.

browserRoute.instruction: Open EventBridge > Rules > Create rule.
Name: fa-monitoring-rule.
Event bus: fa-monitoring-bus.
Rule type: Rule with an event pattern.
Event source: Other.
Choose Custom pattern and paste the supplied fa-monitoring-event-pattern.json.
Select target AWS service > Lambda function.
Function: fa-monitoring-observer.
Configure retry policy so Maximum retry attempts is 0 and Maximum event age is 1 minute where the console exposes these values.
Create the rule.
Confirm the rule is Enabled and the Lambda function is listed as its target.

cliRoute.title: Create the rule, permission and target

expectedResults: fa-monitoring-rule is Enabled on fa-monitoring-bus.
The rule matches source fa.monitoring.demo and detail-type TrainingEvent.
fa-monitoring-observer is the only target.
The Lambda resource policy permits EventBridge to invoke it from the exact rule.

verificationChecks.check: The rule uses fa-monitoring-bus.
The event pattern contains only the training source and detail type.
The target RetryPolicy has MaximumRetryAttempts = 0.
Lambda has the AllowEventBridgeFaMonitoringRule permission statement.

tasks.title: Send three normal events and prove end-to-end delivery
tasks.goal: Send three matching custom events to fa-monitoring-bus and verify EventBridge invokes the observer function three times.
tasks.whyItMatters: The events create the log, trace and custom metric data used by the rest of the Follow Along.
tasks.examRelevance: Event-driven architectures decouple event producers from event-processing targets.

browserRoute.instruction: Keep EventBridge and Lambda open in separate browser tabs.
Use CloudShell with the supplied events file to send the three normal events; the EventBridge console does not need to be used as an event producer for this task.
Open Lambda > fa-monitoring-observer > Monitor.
Confirm Invocations begins to show activity.
Open CloudWatch > Logs > Log groups > /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer.
Open the newest log stream and find three OBSERVABILITY_EVENT status=processed lines.

cliRoute.title: Send the three matching events
cliRoute.content:
cat > fa-monitoring-normal-events.json <<'EOF'
[
  {
    "Source": "fa.monitoring.demo",
    "DetailType": "TrainingEvent",
    "Detail": "{\"message\":\"normal-event-1\",\"forceError\":false}",
    "EventBusName": "fa-monitoring-bus"
  },
  {
    "Source": "fa.monitoring.demo",
    "DetailType": "TrainingEvent",
    "Detail": "{\"message\":\"normal-event-2\",\"forceError\":false}",
    "EventBusName": "fa-monitoring-bus"
  },
  {
    "Source": "fa.monitoring.demo",
    "DetailType": "TrainingEvent",
    "Detail": "{\"message\":\"normal-event-3\",\"forceError\":false}",
    "EventBusName": "fa-monitoring-bus"
  }
]
EOF

aws events put-events   --entries file://fa-monitoring-normal-events.json

aws lambda get-function-configuration   --function-name fa-monitoring-observer   --query '{FunctionName:FunctionName,Tracing:TracingConfig.Mode}'

expectedResults: PutEvents reports FailedEntryCount = 0.
The Lambda is invoked for the matching events.
CloudWatch Logs contains processed log lines.
The function publishes custom metric data for successful events.

verificationChecks.check: FailedEntryCount is 0.
Three processed log entries can be identified.
No forced_error log entry exists yet.

troubleshooting.symptom: PutEvents succeeds but Lambda is not invoked
troubleshooting.fix: Compare Source, DetailType and EventBusName against the rule pattern, then verify the Lambda target and resource-based permission.

tasks.title: Find and graph the FA/Monitoring custom metric
tasks.goal: Locate ProcessedEvents with FunctionName=fa-monitoring-observer and confirm the three successful events produced metric data.
tasks.whyItMatters: Custom metrics let applications publish business or workload signals that built-in AWS metrics cannot know.
tasks.examRelevance: CloudWatch supports AWS service metrics and custom application metrics.
warnings: A newly published custom metric can take a short time to become visible in the metrics browser.

browserRoute.instruction: Open CloudWatch > Metrics > All metrics.
Choose the custom namespace FA/Monitoring.
Choose the FunctionName dimension.
Select ProcessedEvents for fa-monitoring-observer.
Set Statistic to Sum and Period to 1 minute.
Use a recent time range and confirm the graph contains the processed event data.

cliRoute.title: List and read recent custom metric data
cliRoute.content:
aws cloudwatch list-metrics   --namespace FA/Monitoring   --metric-name ProcessedEvents   --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=fa-monitoring-observer

START_TIME=$(date -u -d '15 minutes ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
END_TIME=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics   --namespace FA/Monitoring   --metric-name ProcessedEvents   --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=fa-monitoring-observer   --statistics Sum   --period 60   --start-time "$START_TIME"   --end-time "$END_TIME"

expectedResults: The namespace FA/Monitoring exists.
ProcessedEvents exists with dimension FunctionName=fa-monitoring-observer.
Recent Sum values reflect the successful event processing.

verificationChecks.check: The metric namespace is FA/Monitoring.
The dimension is FunctionName=fa-monitoring-observer.
The metric contains recent non-zero data.

troubleshooting.symptom: The metric is not listed yet
troubleshooting.fix: Use get-metric-statistics with the exact namespace/metric/dimension, and confirm the Lambda execution role allows cloudwatch:PutMetricData for FA/Monitoring.

tasks.title: Create alarms for processed events and Lambda errors
tasks.goal: Create one alarm on the custom ProcessedEvents metric and one alarm on the built-in Lambda Errors metric.
tasks.whyItMatters: Alarms turn metric thresholds into explicit operational states that can later drive notifications or automation.
tasks.examRelevance: CloudWatch alarms evaluate metrics against thresholds and can be combined with other AWS services for automated response.
warnings: No alarm actions are configured, so the lab does not create SNS topics or send notifications.

browserRoute.instruction: Open CloudWatch > Alarms > All alarms > Create alarm.
Select FA/Monitoring > FunctionName > ProcessedEvents for fa-monitoring-observer.
Statistic: Sum. Period: 1 minute.
Threshold type: Static. Condition: Greater/Equal than 3.
Evaluation periods: 1 of 1.
Missing data treatment: Treat missing data as good/not breaching.
Do not configure notification actions.
Name: fa-monitoring-processed-events-alarm and create it.
Create a second alarm using AWS/Lambda > By Function Name > Errors for fa-monitoring-observer.
Statistic: Sum. Period: 1 minute. Threshold: Greater/Equal than 1. Evaluation: 1 of 1. Missing data: not breaching.
Do not configure actions.
Name: fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm and create it.

cliRoute.title: Create both alarms
cliRoute.content:
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm   --alarm-name fa-monitoring-processed-events-alarm   --alarm-description "Training alarm for three or more processed events in one minute"   --namespace FA/Monitoring   --metric-name ProcessedEvents   --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=fa-monitoring-observer   --statistic Sum   --period 60   --evaluation-periods 1   --datapoints-to-alarm 1   --threshold 3   --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold   --treat-missing-data notBreaching

aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm   --alarm-name fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm   --alarm-description "Training alarm for Lambda errors"   --namespace AWS/Lambda   --metric-name Errors   --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=fa-monitoring-observer   --statistic Sum   --period 60   --evaluation-periods 1   --datapoints-to-alarm 1   --threshold 1   --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold   --treat-missing-data notBreaching

aws cloudwatch describe-alarms   --alarm-names fa-monitoring-processed-events-alarm fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm   --query 'MetricAlarms[].{Name:AlarmName,State:StateValue,Metric:MetricName,Namespace:Namespace}'

expectedResults: Both alarms exist.
The custom alarm watches FA/Monitoring ProcessedEvents.
The error alarm watches AWS/Lambda Errors.
Neither alarm has notification actions.

verificationChecks.check: fa-monitoring-processed-events-alarm threshold is 3.
fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm threshold is 1.
Both use one-minute periods and one evaluation period.

tasks.title: Send one controlled error event and observe alarm state changes
tasks.goal: Send a matching event with forceError=true so Lambda records one failure and CloudWatch can evaluate the error alarm.
tasks.whyItMatters: Observability is most useful when you can prove that a failure becomes visible in metrics, logs, alarms and traces.
tasks.examRelevance: CloudWatch metrics and alarms expose unhealthy behavior without requiring manual log inspection alone.
warnings: This is a deliberate application exception in the disposable training function; EventBridge retries are disabled for the target.

browserRoute.instruction: Use CloudShell to send the supplied intentional error event.
Open Lambda > fa-monitoring-observer > Monitor and confirm an Errors data point appears.
Open CloudWatch > Alarms and watch fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm evaluate the failure.
Open /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer and find OBSERVABILITY_EVENT status=forced_error.
Confirm the processed-events custom metric does not increment for the forced error path.

cliRoute.title: Send one intentional error event and inspect alarms
cliRoute.content:
cat > fa-monitoring-error-event.json <<'EOF'
[
  {
    "Source": "fa.monitoring.demo",
    "DetailType": "TrainingEvent",
    "Detail": "{\"message\":\"intentional-error\",\"forceError\":true}",
    "EventBusName": "fa-monitoring-bus"
  }
]
EOF

aws events put-events   --entries file://fa-monitoring-error-event.json

sleep 75

aws cloudwatch describe-alarms   --alarm-names fa-monitoring-processed-events-alarm fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm   --query 'MetricAlarms[].{Name:AlarmName,State:StateValue,Reason:StateReason}'
cliRoute.note: Alarm evaluation is asynchronous; if a state has not updated yet, use the Console graph and describe-alarms again after the next evaluation.

expectedResults: PutEvents reports no failed entries.
Lambda records one controlled application error.
The Lambda Errors metric increases.
fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm can enter ALARM for the failed invocation.
A forced_error log entry exists.

verificationChecks.check: Only one controlled error event was sent.
A Lambda Errors data point is visible.
The log line contains status=forced_error.

troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the EventBridge target RetryPolicy has MaximumRetryAttempts set to 0 and do not send the error event again.

tasks.title: Query Lambda logs with CloudWatch Logs Insights
tasks.goal: Run one detail query and one aggregate query against the Lambda log group to separate processed and forced-error events.
tasks.whyItMatters: Logs Insights can search and aggregate large log sets without manually opening individual log streams.
tasks.examRelevance: CloudWatch Logs supports centralized query and troubleshooting workflows.
warnings: Use the narrow 15-minute time range and only the one training log group to reduce unnecessary query scanning.

browserRoute.instruction: Open CloudWatch > Logs > Logs Insights.
Select only /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer.
Set the time range to the last 15 minutes.
Run: fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /OBSERVABILITY_EVENT/ | sort @timestamp desc | limit 20
Confirm processed and forced_error records appear.
Run: filter @message like /OBSERVABILITY_EVENT/ | parse @message /status=(?<status>[^ ]+)/ | stats count(*) as events by status
Confirm the result groups events by processed and forced_error status.
Stop/cancel any still-running query before leaving the page.

cliRoute.title: Run the detail and aggregate queries
cliRoute.content:
START=$(date -d '15 minutes ago' +%s)
END=$(date +%s)

DETAIL_QUERY_ID=$(aws logs start-query \
  --log-group-name /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer \
  --start-time "$START" \
  --end-time "$END" \
  --query-string 'fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /OBSERVABILITY_EVENT/ | sort @timestamp desc | limit 20' \
  --query queryId \
  --output text)

sleep 3
aws logs get-query-results --query-id "$DETAIL_QUERY_ID"

AGG_QUERY_ID=$(aws logs start-query \
  --log-group-name /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer \
  --start-time "$START" \
  --end-time "$END" \
  --query-string 'filter @message like /OBSERVABILITY_EVENT/ | parse @message /status=(?<status>[^ ]+)/ | stats count(*) as events by status' \
  --query queryId \
  --output text)

sleep 3
aws logs get-query-results --query-id "$AGG_QUERY_ID"

expectedResults: The detail query returns recent OBSERVABILITY_EVENT lines.
The aggregate query separates processed from forced_error status values.

verificationChecks.check: The query scope includes only /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer.
Processed events are returned.
The forced error is returned.
The stats query groups by status.

troubleshooting.fix: Run get-query-results again for the same query ID after it finishes; do not start duplicate queries unnecessarily.

tasks.title: Inspect successful and failed Lambda traces in AWS X-Ray
tasks.goal: Use the X-Ray trace view and API to find traces for fa-monitoring-observer and distinguish a successful trace from the controlled failure.
tasks.whyItMatters: Metrics show that something changed, logs show application messages, and traces show the execution path and timing for individual requests.
tasks.examRelevance: X-Ray is used to trace distributed requests and troubleshoot latency/errors across supported services.
warnings: X-Ray uses sampling, so not every invocation is guaranteed to produce a stored trace.

browserRoute.instruction: Open CloudWatch > X-Ray traces or the AWS X-Ray trace view for eu-west-2.
Set the time range to include the events sent in this Follow Along.
Filter for service fa-monitoring-observer where the console provides a service filter.
Open a successful trace and inspect duration and the Lambda segment.
Open a trace containing the controlled error if sampled and inspect its fault/error indicators.
Confirm Active tracing remains enabled on fa-monitoring-observer.

cliRoute.title: List recent X-Ray trace summaries for the function
cliRoute.content:
XRAY_START=$(date -u -d '30 minutes ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
XRAY_END=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

aws xray get-trace-summaries   --start-time "$XRAY_START"   --end-time "$XRAY_END"   --filter-expression 'service("fa-monitoring-observer")'   --query 'TraceSummaries[].{Id:Id,Duration:Duration,HasError:HasError,HasFault:HasFault}'   --max-items 20

expectedResults: Recent trace summaries can be found for the function when invocations were sampled.
Successful traces show normal execution.
A sampled controlled failure can show an error/fault signal.

verificationChecks.check: Lambda tracing mode is Active.
At least one sampled trace can be inspected after repeated normal test events if necessary.
You can explain the difference between metrics, logs and traces.

troubleshooting.fix: Confirm Active tracing and AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess, then send additional normal training events because X-Ray sampling does not store every invocation.

tasks.title: Review the complete observability flow and exam decisions
tasks.goal: Trace one event from EventBridge through Lambda into logs, custom metrics, alarms and X-Ray and identify what each service contributes.
tasks.whyItMatters: The value of observability comes from combining signals rather than treating logs, metrics and traces as isolated tools.
tasks.examRelevance: SAA-C03 questions often test which service or signal best solves a specific monitoring or event-routing requirement.

browserRoute.instruction: Open EventBridge and confirm fa-monitoring-bus and fa-monitoring-rule route matching events to fa-monitoring-observer.
Open Lambda monitoring and identify Invocations and Errors.
Open CloudWatch custom metrics and identify FA/Monitoring ProcessedEvents.
Open CloudWatch alarms and identify the processed-events and Lambda-errors alarms.
Open Logs Insights and identify application messages for both successful and failed events.
Open X-Ray and identify request-level traces.
Review the decision map: EventBridge routes events; CloudWatch metrics quantify behavior; alarms evaluate thresholds; Logs Insights searches log events; X-Ray traces individual requests.

cliRoute.title: Run a non-destructive inventory
cliRoute.content:
aws events describe-event-bus --name fa-monitoring-bus
aws events describe-rule --name fa-monitoring-rule --event-bus-name fa-monitoring-bus
aws lambda get-function-configuration   --function-name fa-monitoring-observer   --query '{Name:FunctionName,Tracing:TracingConfig.Mode,Role:Role}'
aws cloudwatch list-metrics   --namespace FA/Monitoring   --metric-name ProcessedEvents
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms   --alarm-names fa-monitoring-processed-events-alarm fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm   --query 'MetricAlarms[].{Name:AlarmName,State:StateValue}'

expectedResults: The complete event-to-observability chain is visible.
Each AWS service has a distinct role in the design.
All resources are still present immediately before cleanup.

verificationChecks.check: You can explain EventBridge versus CloudWatch.
You can explain metrics versus logs versus traces.
You can explain why an alarm is built on a metric rather than directly on an X-Ray trace.

tasks.title: Delete alarms, EventBridge routing, Lambda and log resources in reverse order
tasks.goal: Delete the monitoring and event-driven resources in dependency-safe order while retaining the administrator account.
tasks.whyItMatters: The rule must stop targeting Lambda before the function is removed, and temporary observability resources should not remain after the lab.
tasks.examRelevance: Dependency-aware cleanup reinforces how EventBridge, Lambda and CloudWatch resources relate to one another.
warnings: These steps are destructive. Delete only resources with the exact fa-monitoring names from this Follow Along.

browserRoute.instruction: CloudWatch: delete fa-monitoring-processed-events-alarm and fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm.
EventBridge: open fa-monitoring-rule, remove fa-monitoring-observer as its target, then delete fa-monitoring-rule.
EventBridge: delete fa-monitoring-bus after the rule is gone.
Lambda: delete fa-monitoring-observer.
CloudWatch Logs: delete /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer.
IAM: open fa-monitoring-lambda-role.
Detach AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole and AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess.
Delete inline policy fa-monitoring-metric-policy.
Delete fa-monitoring-lambda-role.
Do not delete or modify the existing administrator account.

cliRoute.title: Delete cloud resources in reverse dependency order
cliRoute.content:
aws cloudwatch delete-alarms   --alarm-names fa-monitoring-processed-events-alarm fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm

aws events remove-targets   --rule fa-monitoring-rule   --event-bus-name fa-monitoring-bus   --ids fa-monitoring-lambda-target

aws lambda remove-permission   --function-name fa-monitoring-observer   --statement-id AllowEventBridgeFaMonitoringRule

aws events delete-rule   --name fa-monitoring-rule   --event-bus-name fa-monitoring-bus

aws events delete-event-bus --name fa-monitoring-bus

aws lambda delete-function --function-name fa-monitoring-observer

aws logs delete-log-group   --log-group-name /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer

aws iam detach-role-policy   --role-name fa-monitoring-lambda-role   --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole

aws iam detach-role-policy   --role-name fa-monitoring-lambda-role   --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess

aws iam delete-role-policy   --role-name fa-monitoring-lambda-role   --policy-name fa-monitoring-metric-policy

aws iam delete-role --role-name fa-monitoring-lambda-role

cliRoute.title: Verify the named resources are gone
cliRoute.content:
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms   --alarm-names fa-monitoring-processed-events-alarm fa-monitoring-lambda-errors-alarm

aws events list-event-buses   --query "EventBuses[?Name=='fa-monitoring-bus']"

aws lambda get-function   --function-name fa-monitoring-observer

aws logs describe-log-groups   --log-group-name-prefix /aws/lambda/fa-monitoring-observer

aws iam get-role --role-name fa-monitoring-lambda-role
cliRoute.note: Expected: alarm list is empty; event bus query is empty; Lambda and IAM role report not found; the exact Lambda log group is absent.

expectedResults: Both alarms are absent.
fa-monitoring-rule and fa-monitoring-bus are absent.
fa-monitoring-observer is absent.
The Lambda log group is absent.
fa-monitoring-lambda-role is absent.
The existing administrator account remains unchanged.

verificationChecks.check: No fa-monitoring alarm remains.
No fa-monitoring custom event bus or rule remains.
No fa-monitoring Lambda function or log group remains.
No fa-monitoring Lambda role remains.

troubleshooting.symptom: EventBridge rule deletion fails because targets remain
troubleshooting.fix: Run remove-targets for fa-monitoring-lambda-target first, then delete the rule.
Confirm both managed policies are detached and fa-monitoring-metric-policy is deleted before deleting the role.

tasks.title: Remove CloudShell helper files and acknowledge programme cleanup
tasks.goal: Delete only the helper files created in CloudShell and complete the final cleanup acknowledgement.
tasks.whyItMatters: Temporary JSON, Python and ZIP files should be removed after the AWS resources they describe are gone.
tasks.examRelevance: Operational hygiene includes removing temporary deployment artifacts after use.
warnings: Delete only the exact fa-monitoring helper files listed here; do not clear unrelated CloudShell files.

browserRoute.instruction: Return to AWS CloudShell.
List the current directory and identify only files beginning with fa-monitoring plus lambda_function.py.
Run the cleanup command supplied below.
List the directory again and confirm the training helper files are gone.
Close CloudShell when finished; the administrator account itself remains in place.

cliRoute.title: Remove only the lab helper files
cliRoute.content:
rm -f   fa-monitoring-lambda-trust.json   fa-monitoring-metric-policy.json   lambda_function.py   fa-monitoring-observer.zip   fa-monitoring-event-pattern.json   fa-monitoring-targets.json   fa-monitoring-normal-events.json   fa-monitoring-error-event.json

ls -la | grep -E 'fa-monitoring|lambda_function.py' || true

expectedResults: The exact helper files are absent from CloudShell.
The administrator account remains available.
The programme cleanup acknowledgement can be made truthfully.

verificationChecks.check: No listed fa-monitoring helper file remains.
All cloud cleanup checks from Task 14 passed.
The administrator account was not deleted or modified.

Delete only the exact JSON, Python and ZIP files created by the lab.
